extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to NIH grant programs (those with applications reviewed by CSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes what happens to an NIH grant application during and after peer review managed by the Center for Scientific Review (CSR), including reviewer assignment, pre-meeting critiques and scores, meeting procedures, scoring, results release, and institute-level actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment and SRO responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the meeting, reviewers are assigned to your application. Your scientific review officer (SRO) is your main contact while your application is under peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO will analyze the content of your application, check for completeness and compliance with policies, and decide which reviewers can best evaluate it. Reviewers have access to your application approximately 6 weeks before the scientific review group meeting. Each application is assigned to three or more reviewers, and at least two of them provide full written critiques. These assigned reviewers lead the discussion at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary critiques and preliminary scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the scientific review group meets, the assigned reviewers confidentially submit preliminary critiques. Reviewers also assign preliminary scores for each review criterion and for the overall impact of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These preliminary critiques and scores are used by the SRO and to inform which applications will be discussed at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preliminary overall impact scores to select discussed applications (triage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO then uses the preliminary overall impact scores to generate a preliminary list of applications to be discussed. Applications in the lower half are not typically discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review order for the discussed applications is random.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review meeting convening, chair, and SRO (DFO) role
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific review group is convened for 1 to 2 days. One member serves as chair and facilitates the discussion. The SRO serves as the designated federal official and acts as a steward of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO ensures policy and procedures are followed, and captures score-driving points for each discussed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest management during discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: For each application under discussion, any review group members who are in conflict with the application leave the room before discussion begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicted members do not participate in the discussion or scoring for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of assigned and mail reviews; group discussion participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers present their evaluations and any mail reviews are read. Discussion is opened to the review group, as those beyond the assigned reviewers also have expertise in the topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers lead but the broader group may contribute substantive points that affect scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final scoring practice after discussion (overall impact scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: After discussion, all reviewers at the meeting privately submit overall impact scores to CSR. The review outcome is a decision based on the assessment of all members of the scientific review group, not only that of the assigned reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall impact scores submitted privately by all non-conflicted reviewers determine the final ranked outcome used for subsequent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results released to applicants (priority score, percentile, summary statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a few days after the meeting, your priority score and percentile ranking (if applicable) are available to you via your eRA Commons account. In most cases, your summary statement will be available via eRA Commons within a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement will include the written critiques provided by the assigned reviewers, the SRO’s summary of the discussion, scores for each review criterion, and administrative notes of special consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome for applications not discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application was not discussed, you will receive the critiques of the assigned reviewers and preliminary scores for each review criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-discussed applications do not receive the full meeting discussion SRO summary but do receive assigned reviewers' critiques and their preliminary criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned institute program officer post-review role
rubrics_metrics.description: After the review, a program officer (PO) at the funding institute to which your application has been assigned will be your main point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO may help interpret your review results and give you guidance in preparing a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level advisory council review for institute relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: In a second level of review, the advisory council of the funding institute/center will consider the peer review outcomes and determine the relevance of your proposed research to the institute/center’s priorities and public health needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council review focuses on programmatic relevance and alignment with institute priorities rather than re-evaluating scientific peer review criteria.
